entities.summary: Bolivia is a sovereign nation in South America, Americas. Its capital is Sucre (constitutional/judicial); La Paz (seat of government/executive). Official languages include Spanish, Quechua, Aymara. Government: Unitary presidential constitutional republic (Plurinational State). Population: approximately 12.4 million. Area: 1,098,581 km². Comprehensive index for Bolivia covering Tiwanaku civilization, Aymara kingdoms, Inca Kollasuyu, Potosí silver mountain (richest city in the world, mita forced labor, ~8 million dead), Túpac Katari rebellion, independence 1825 (named for Bolívar), War of the Pacific 1879-84 (lost coast), Chaco War 1932-35, 1952 National Revolution, Che Guevara killed 1967, Evo Morales (first indigenous president), coca/cocaine politics, and lithium reserves.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bolivia's rich history includes the Tiwanaku civilization and the Túpac Katari rebellion, which had significant regional impact in South America. The country's lithium reserves also have global economic implications.
